tone_patterns: Technical, standards-led tone that references recognized frameworks and protocols to anchor credibility
Balanced narrative that combines methodological detail with plain-language rationale for choices and limitations
Cautious, qualified language when discussing estimates, uncertainty, and comparability over time
Forward-looking improvement framing (process enhancements, automation, data quality uplift) without overstating outcomes
Governance-aware tone that links calculations to internal ownership, review, and oversight roles
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a purpose statement describing what is being measured and why it matters for monitoring and decision-making
Early placement of the measurement framework and boundary approach before presenting any results
Uses short lead-in sentences followed by bullet lists to define inclusion criteria, scope dimensions, and exclusions
Methodology paragraphs explain calculation inputs and edge-case handling (e.g., illiquidity, negative equity) as discrete rules
Includes a cross-reference sentence pointing readers to a later subsection for formulas/calculation approach
Introduces a time reference for the measurement snapshot (as-of date) as a standalone sentence
Presents limitations and sources of variability in a dedicated paragraph (regulatory changes, data quality, methodology updates, market movements)
Concludes with a capability/governance paragraph describing teams, approvals, controls, and system/process improvements
Ends with a principle-based disclosure choice paragraph explaining aggregation level and potential future granularity
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection heading format (e.g., section.subsection) paired with an action-oriented title describing management of a specific exposure
Uses a consistent section footer/header label indicating the broader report section (e.g., 'Metrics and targets')
Employs quoted subheading references within text to point to internal subsections (e.g., a named methodology/calculation appendix within the section)
table_patterns: No tables in the excerpt; quantitative highlights are embedded as callouts rather than tabulated
Where lists function as pseudo-tables, bullets are used to enumerate scope dimensions and exclusions with parallel phrasing
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No charts/figures shown; instead, a numeric highlight is presented as a standalone callout block
Uses a symbol marker adjacent to a metric to indicate assurance coverage, functioning like a visual annotation
pdf_layout_patterns: Page begins with a prominent subsection heading followed by multi-paragraph narrative in a single main column
Bulleted lists are indented with generous line spacing to improve scanability of criteria and exclusions
A right-side (or offset) callout box contains key quantitative outputs and portfolio scoping context, visually separated from the main text
Assurance-related content is separated into a distinct boxed or inset note area, preceded by a symbol legend (e.g., Δ) to explain markings
Footer includes section label, page number, and report title/identifier in a consistent placement
Symbol markers (e.g., Δ) are used inline near metrics and repeated in the assurance note to connect the claim to the assurance scope
disclosure_language_patterns: Defines boundaries explicitly using a named consolidation approach and ties it to a recognized protocol
States scope coverage using standardized emissions taxonomy (e.g., scope/category language) and clarifies what is included/excluded
Uses 'best-effort' style qualifiers when disclosure is constrained by regulation or data availability
Explains comparability constraints and why year-on-year movements may not reflect underlying performance
Documents methodological choices (e.g., absolute reporting vs disaggregation) and provides rationale tied to data quality
Provides a pathway statement indicating potential future enhancement of granularity as data improves
Includes external references to where detailed methodology/basis of reporting can be found (e.g., corporate website document)
evidence_presentation_patterns: Framework citation used as methodological evidence (naming the standard and how it is applied)
Assurance evidence presented via a symbol-tagging system and an accompanying assurance scope note
Assurance note specifies assurance level, applicable assurance standards, and where the full opinion can be accessed
Governance evidence provided by naming internal functions responsible for calculation and approval (role-based, not person-based)
Method evidence includes explicit rule statements for special cases (e.g., illiquid pricing, negative equity handling)
section_specific_observations: The section blends 'metrics' with 'methodology narrative'—results are secondary to explaining scoping, boundaries, and calculation rules
Scoping is presented as a structured funnel: inclusion criteria → boundary definition → scope dimensions → exclusions → limitations → governance
Assurance is treated as a modular disclosure element that can be reused across metrics via consistent symbol marking
The narrative distinguishes between portfolio scoping (what is assessed) and calculation mechanics (how it is computed), with explicit signposting
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, subsidiary references, or portfolio composition specifics
Any currency amounts, portfolio totals, emissions totals, dates, thresholds, percentages, or other numeric values
Any named assurance provider, website links, or document titles
Any internal team names, job titles, or governance role labels that could identify the reference organization
Any sector lists or asset-class lists presented as the reference company’s specific scope (retain only the pattern of listing categories)
Any claims implying performance, leadership, or commitments that are specific to the reference company
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Specific frameworks/protocol names and standards identifiers (treated as content-specific references even though the pattern is reusable)
Assurance provider name and assurance opinion availability statement
Exact asset class examples and sector inclusion details
All numeric thresholds, portfolio values, emissions quantities, percentages, and as-of dates
Specific internal function/team names and approval roles
Specific document title for methodology/basis of reporting and any website reference
